title: Img2threejs and Codex experiments
author: notpls
selftext: Played around a bit with img2threejs and Codex, and I really liked the results. I couldn’t get anything this polished with Blender MCP.

replies.author: notpls
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/ism8sg1weceh1.png?width=1536&format=png&auto=webp&s=9d68e374c76c84145bbb6f19de09768563c63755

I made the image in ChatGPT.

Then I gave Codex this link: [https://github.com/hoainho/img2threejs](https://github.com/hoainho/img2threejs) and asked it to add the skill to a new project. After that, I gave it the image and used this prompt:

`/img2threejs Rebuild this object as a Three.js model, keeping the proportions, angles, and colours.`

Then came half a day of lazy tweaking, basically just telling it what I didn’t like.

And here’s the result.

comments.author: shottycoin
comments.body: actually tried img2threejs, it costs ridiculous amount just for one simple model. with GPT 5.6 Sol. Around 6 bucks. and the result was not that impressive. it needs to be cost optimized. remesh ai gen mesh makes more sense for now.

replies.author: notpls
replies.body: I don’t know how much it actually cost me since I have a subscription. But there’s an important difference here: this is threejs code, which gives you much more room to experiment with reuse, procedural architecture, and so on.

replies.author: shottycoin
replies.body: yea I used it with API through Openrouter. it costs a lot on my case. with subscription I haven't checked yet. token cost was over 200K total.

replies.author: shottycoin
replies.body: However if we can achieve these models with less token burn, it'd a lot better to use than 3D mesh generation ofc.
